pr.title: Remove a finished pull request from a loop through the CLI
pr.head: b71f1abfa7b9f108eabc230ba9167d9cb5b11f7e

summary: A watch loop or a review loop keeps the pull requests it works on in a tracked file: a plain text file the loop's watcher script re-reads every cycle, with one owner/repo#number per line. A line that starts with !, such as !acme/app#12, is an exclusion: it keeps that pull request out of the loop wherever it sits in the file. Two CLI commands already changed the file: project loop drop appends an exclusion, and project loop restore deletes one.

One write was still done by hand. When a pull request merged or closed, the loop skills told the agent running the loop to delete the pull request's line from the file itself. This change adds project loop remove owner/repo#number --tracked <file> for that step, and points every skill instruction, watcher comment, and document at it.

CommandLines it changesWhen a loop runs it
dropAppends !owner/repo#numberTo keep an open pull request out
restoreDeletes the ! linesTo let a dropped pull request back in
remove (new)Deletes the plain lines, keeps the ! linesWhen a pull request merges or closes

remove leaves exclusions alone on purpose. The review loop's watcher adopts the operator's open pull requests by appending any that the file does not name, and it treats an exclusion as naming one. If remove also deleted the exclusion, a pull request the user had dropped would be adopted again if it ever reopened.

cards.html:

cards.title: What the change leaves for later
cards.html:
• Appending a pull request to a tracked file still has no command; the implement skill tells the loop to append the line itself.
  • Exclusions for closed pull requests stay in the file. Only restore deletes them.

groups.title: The remove command
groups.kicker: A third project loop command that forgets a finished pull request
intro: src/projector/loop.py holds the tracked-file commands. Before this change, restore read the file, kept every line that was not an exclusion for the pull request, and wrote the rest back through write_through, the repository's atomic rewrite that swaps in a temporary file and keeps the original's mode and any symlink. That body is now rewrite_without, which takes the line test as an argument, and restore and remove each pass their own test: is_exclusion for ! lines, and the new is_entry for plain lines.

is_entry trims the line and compares it to the reference without regard to case. That matches how both watcher scripts read an entry, so remove deletes exactly the lines a watcher would have tracked. When no line matches, the file is not rewritten at all.
In src/projector/cli.py, run_loop replaces its drop-or-restore branches with one table keyed by the subcommand, giving each command its function, its --json action, and its two messages.

checks.text: The six new RemoveTests and the existing drop and restore tests all pass on this head. A manual run against a symlinked tracked file rewrote the link's target and kept the link.

files.note: Adds is_entry and remove, and turns restore's body into the shared rewrite_without.

checks.text: A watcher may append a line it adopted while this rewrite runs, and the rename would then lose that line. restore had the same window at the base, and the hand edit this replaces had it too. The review watcher re-adopts a lost line on its next cycle, because it appends every open pull request the file does not name.
The docstring states why exclusions survive: a review loop would otherwise adopt a dropped pull request again if it reopened.

files.note: Registers remove and folds the three commands' output into one table in run_loop.

checks.text: drop and restore print the same text and the same --json actions as at the base; unchanged still replaces the action when nothing changed.

files.note: Covers case-insensitive removal with mode kept, exclusions left in place, an unlisted pull request leaving the file untouched (same inode), --json for both actions, and exit codes 65 and 66.

groups.title: Loop skills and watchers
groups.kicker: Every place that told a loop to delete a line by hand now runs the command
intro: Two skills run loops over a tracked file: start-watch-loop, which fixes review findings on pull requests, and start-review-loop, which reviews each new head. Both told the agent to delete a merged or closed pull request's line from the file. Each of those instructions now runs project loop remove owner/repo#number --tracked <file>, and each skill's description of the tracked file names all three commands and says how they differ.

The watcher scripts change only in comments and one message. Their header comments say the loop removes a merged pull request with project loop remove. The review watcher's CLOSED event, which reports a tracked pull request that is no longer open, now ends "remove it from the tracked file" instead of "drop it", because drop is the command that keeps an open pull request out.

checks.text: A search of the head finds no remaining instruction to delete a tracked line by hand or to drop a closed pull request.

files.note: The scope paragraph, step 6, the CLOSED bullet, and "Continue after fixes" run project loop remove.

checks.text: The claim that adoption never brings a dropped pull request back holds: adopt in watch-prs.sh skips any pull request a ! line names.

files.note: Step 4, the merged-pull-request bullet, the idle-file paragraph, and the DONE check run project loop remove.

checks.text: The loop skills read this text as an instruction, so the wording now names the action that matches remove.
